services.name: Google Drive
services.description: Store and sync your files with Google Drive

setupSteps.title: Go to Google Cloud Console
setupSteps.description: Open Google Cloud Console and log in with your Google account
setupSteps.action: Visit https://console.cloud.google.com
setupSteps.details: Make sure you're logged in with the Google account you want to use for your service

setupSteps.title: Select Your Project
setupSteps.description: Choose your project or create a new one
setupSteps.action: Click the project dropdown at the top
setupSteps.details: If you don't have a project, click 'New Project' and follow the setup wizard

setupSteps.title: Enable APIs
setupSteps.description: Enable the Google Drive API for your project
setupSteps.action: Go to APIs & Services → Library
setupSteps.details: Search for 'Google Drive API' and click 'Enable'

setupSteps.title: Create OAuth 2.0 Credentials
setupSteps.description: Create OAuth 2.0 client ID for your application
setupSteps.action: Navigate to APIs & Services → Credentials
setupSteps.details: Click 'Create Credentials' → 'OAuth 2.0 Client ID', choose 'Web application' type

setupSteps.title: Configure OAuth Consent Screen
setupSteps.description: Set up the OAuth consent screen for your application
setupSteps.action: Go to OAuth consent screen and configure your app details
setupSteps.details: Add your app name, user support email, and authorized domains

setupSteps.title: Add Redirect URI
setupSteps.description: Configure the redirect URI for OAuth callback
setupSteps.action: In your OAuth client, add redirect URI: http://localhost:9090/api/drive/oauth/callback
setupSteps.details: This URI will handle the OAuth callback after user authorization

setupSteps.title: Get Client Credentials
setupSteps.description: Copy your Client ID and Client Secret
setupSteps.action: In your OAuth client, copy the Client ID and Client Secret
setupSteps.details: You'll need these credentials to configure FileVault

troubleshooting.solution: Make sure Google Drive API is enabled in your Google Cloud Console
Verify your OAuth 2.0 credentials are correct in Google Cloud Console
Ensure the redirect URI in your OAuth client matches: http://localhost:9090/api/drive/oauth/callback
Complete the OAuth consent screen setup in Google Cloud Console

services.name: Dropbox
services.description: Secure file storage and sharing with Dropbox

setupSteps.title: Create Dropbox App
setupSteps.description: Go to Dropbox App Console and create a new app
setupSteps.action: Visit https://www.dropbox.com/developers/apps
setupSteps.details: Click 'Create app' and choose 'Scoped access' for better security

setupSteps.title: Configure App Settings
setupSteps.description: Set up your app permissions and settings
setupSteps.action: In your app dashboard, go to 'Permissions' tab
setupSteps.details: Enable 'files.metadata.write' and 'files.content.write' permissions

setupSteps.title: Generate Access Token
setupSteps.description: Create an access token for your app
setupSteps.action: Go to 'Settings' tab and click 'Generate access token'
setupSteps.details: Copy the generated token - you'll need this for FileVault

setupSteps.title: Add Token to FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your access token in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Paste the token in the configuration form below
setupSteps.details: The token will be encrypted and stored securely

troubleshooting.solution: Generate a new access token from your Dropbox app console
Check that your app has the required permissions enabled

setupSteps.title: Register App in Azure
setupSteps.description: Create an app registration in Azure Active Directory
setupSteps.action: Go to https://portal.azure.com → Azure Active Directory → App registrations
setupSteps.details: Click 'New registration' and enter your app details

setupSteps.title: Configure API Permissions
setupSteps.description: Add Microsoft Graph permissions for OneDrive
setupSteps.action: In your app, go to 'API permissions' → 'Add a permission'
setupSteps.details: Add 'Files.ReadWrite' and 'User.Read' permissions

setupSteps.title: Generate Client Secret
setupSteps.description: Create a client secret for authentication
setupSteps.action: Go to 'Certificates & secrets' → 'New client secret'
setupSteps.details: Copy the secret value - you'll need this for FileVault

setupSteps.title: Configure FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your app details in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Fill in the Client ID and Client Secret below
setupSteps.details: These will be used to authenticate with OneDrive

troubleshooting.solution: Verify your Client ID and Secret are correct
Check that your app has the required Graph API permissions

services.name: Amazon S3
services.description: Scalable cloud storage with Amazon S3

setupSteps.title: Create AWS Account
setupSteps.description: Sign up for Amazon Web Services
setupSteps.action: Visit https://aws.amazon.com and create an account
setupSteps.details: You'll need a credit card for verification, but S3 has a free tier

setupSteps.title: Create S3 Bucket
setupSteps.description: Create a new S3 bucket for your files
setupSteps.action: Go to S3 console and click 'Create bucket'
setupSteps.details: Choose a unique bucket name and select your preferred region

setupSteps.title: Create IAM User
setupSteps.description: Create a user with S3 access permissions
setupSteps.action: Go to IAM → Users → Create user
setupSteps.details: Attach the 'AmazonS3FullAccess' policy to the user

setupSteps.title: Generate Access Keys
setupSteps.description: Create access keys for the IAM user
setupSteps.action: In your user, go to 'Security credentials' → 'Create access key'
setupSteps.details: Download the CSV file with your Access Key ID and Secret

setupSteps.title: Configure FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your AWS credentials in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Fill in the Access Key ID, Secret Key, and Bucket name below
setupSteps.details: These will be encrypted and stored securely

requirements: Access Key ID and Secret Key

troubleshooting.solution: Check that your IAM user has S3 permissions
Verify the bucket name and region are correct

services.name: GitHub
services.description: Version control and code storage with GitHub

setupSteps.title: Create GitHub Account
setupSteps.description: Sign up for a GitHub account if you don't have one
setupSteps.action: Visit https://github.com and create an account
setupSteps.details: Choose a username and verify your email address

setupSteps.title: Generate Personal Access Token
setupSteps.description: Create a token for API access
setupSteps.action: Go to Settings → Developer settings → Personal access tokens
setupSteps.details: Click 'Generate new token' and select 'repo' scope

setupSteps.title: Create Repository
setupSteps.description: Create a new repository for your files
setupSteps.action: Click 'New repository' on GitHub
setupSteps.details: Choose a name and make it private for security

setupSteps.title: Configure FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your GitHub details in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Fill in your username, token, and repository name below
setupSteps.details: The token will be encrypted and stored securely

troubleshooting.solution: Check that your personal access token is valid
Verify the repository name and that you have access

services.name: Backblaze B2
services.description: Low-cost cloud storage with Backblaze B2

setupSteps.title: Create Backblaze Account
setupSteps.description: Sign up for a Backblaze B2 account
setupSteps.action: Visit https://www.backblaze.com/b2/cloud-storage.html
setupSteps.details: Create an account and verify your email address

setupSteps.title: Create B2 Bucket
setupSteps.description: Create a new B2 bucket for your files
setupSteps.action: Go to B2 Cloud Storage and click 'Create a Bucket'
setupSteps.details: Choose a unique bucket name and select your preferred region

setupSteps.title: Create Application Key
setupSteps.description: Generate an application key for API access
setupSteps.action: Go to 'App Keys' and click 'Add a New Application Key'
setupSteps.details: Give it a name and select the bucket you created

setupSteps.title: Configure FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your B2 credentials in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Fill in the Application Key ID and Application Key below
setupSteps.details: These will be encrypted and stored securely

troubleshooting.solution: Check that your application key has the correct permissions
Verify the bucket name and that it exists in your B2 account

setupSteps.title: Create Azure Account
setupSteps.description: Sign up for Microsoft Azure
setupSteps.action: Visit https://azure.microsoft.com and create an account
setupSteps.details: You'll need a credit card for verification, but Azure has a free tier

setupSteps.title: Create Storage Account
setupSteps.description: Create a new Azure Storage Account
setupSteps.action: Go to Azure Portal → Storage accounts → Create
setupSteps.details: Choose a unique name and select your preferred region

setupSteps.title: Create Container
setupSteps.description: Create a blob container in your storage account
setupSteps.action: In your storage account, go to 'Containers' and click 'Add container'
setupSteps.details: Choose a name for your container and set the access level

setupSteps.title: Get Access Keys
setupSteps.description: Retrieve your storage account access keys
setupSteps.action: Go to 'Access keys' in your storage account settings
setupSteps.details: Copy the key1 or key2 - you'll need this for FileVault

setupSteps.title: Configure FileVault
setupSteps.description: Enter your Azure credentials in FileVault
setupSteps.action: Fill in the Account Name, Access Key, and Container name below
setupSteps.details: These will be encrypted and stored securely

troubleshooting.solution: Check that your access key is correct and has the necessary permissions
Verify the container name and that it exists in your storage account
